To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The large N effective actions of the nonlinear sigma models with O(N + 4)/O(N) and O(N + 5)/O(N) cosets, which are the simplest models that can accommodate the I = 1/2 and 3/2 pion scattering data, respectively, have been derived in the framework of chiral perturbation.

we have found a new mechanism to stabilize the skyrmion, which is based on the inclusion of a new counter term in the chiral perturbation series, that we have shown that the skyrmion becomes stable for pion masses above 500 MeV, that we have calculated the mass of the skyrmionic baryon, that we have obtained the pion mass dependence of the pion-nucleon coupling constant, and that we have shown the existence of a critical pion mass

the large N effective action for the non-linear sigma-model based on the coset O (N + 1)/ O (N), with N > 3, can be renormalized at the two-loop level by means of a finite number of counter terms and the resulting theory can be used to describe the I = J pion-pion scattering in the low-energy limit.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the low energy properties of the non-linear σ-model.
the study of the pion scattering in the large N expansion of chiral perturbation.
the application of chiral perturbation techniques to low-energy hadron physics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the non-local chiral Lagrangian is a useful tool to study the properties and the interactions of pions in the energy region of the order of the pion mass, but not to study the properties or the interactions of baryons.
the chiral perturbation approach is very useful for studying the properties of the pion scattering but is not suitable for the study of the skyrmions.

chiral perturbation theories with a large number of pions are a good approximation to low-energy pion physics, but that they are not good enough to describe the pion-nucleon interaction and the nucleon structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the large N effective action for the non-linear sigma-model is a useful approximation for the pion scattering at low energies but it is not adequate to describe the properties of the baryon.
the large N effective action for pion scattering is well behaved and it is possible to fit the experimental data with a finite number of coupling constants.
the non-locality of the effective theory is a necessary ingredient for a consistent description of the skyrmions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the non-linear sigma models based in O(N + 2)/O(N) are not renormalizable.

the large N effective action for the non-linear sigma-model with an infinite number of pion fields, which is the simplest example of a non-renormalizable theory, is not a good effective field theory for low-energy pion-pion scattering.
, for a large class of theories, the renormalized non-local effective action can be used to describe low-energy pion dynamics and to calculate physical quantities.
